subject: FM
stem: Cancer patient asks doctor not to tell family. Doctor respects her wishes. Which principle is applied?
explanation: Recall: confidentiality/autonomy – competent adult controls disclosure. Breach only for serious harm/public safety per law.

subject: FM
stem: Child critically ill, parents refuse life-saving treatment, want religious healer only. Best?
options: B. Engage respectfully + bring trusted religious leader + ethics + seek legal authorisation to save life; never abandon
explanation: Paediatric emergency: best interests override refusal. Culturally sensitive engagement + ethics/legal + document. Life-threatening = court order if needed.

subject: FM
stem: Radiologist almost filed report for wrong patient but caught before submitting. Event type?
options: B. Near miss – no harm due to catch; report + systems fix
explanation: Near miss: error intercepted. Report to patient-safety system, disclose per policy, fix ID checks/barcoding.

subject: FM
stem: Doctor dismissed serious rash as normal despite nurse concern; patient discharged, returned and died. Error type?
options: B. Negligence/malpractice – breach of duty + harm
explanation: Ignoring red flags + hierarchy failure → harm. Classic negligence: duty, breach, causation, damages. Needs disclosure + review.

explanation: SPIKES + privacy + empathy + clear plan + support person + written summary.

subject: FM
stem: Elderly independent woman falls, no injury. Most useful next step?
options: A. Move to nursing home immediately
B. Medication review + orthostatic vitals + vision/balance/home hazards + bone health
explanation: Recall: meds review first (sedatives, antihypertensives). Then gait, vision, footwear, home safety, vitamin D/calcium, physio.

subject: FM
stem: Hypertensive on nitrates + alpha-blocker, recurrent syncope, normal ECG, no chest pain/palpitations/SOB. Most likely cause?
explanation: Recall: drug-induced orthostasis. Check lying/standing BP, review meds, hydrate, compression, deprescribe.

subject: FM
stem: Asymptomatic, prior chest pain/syncope, exam normal. Best cardiac test?
options: B. Exercise stress test (± imaging) to unmask ischaemia/arrhythmia
explanation: Recall: exertional syncope/chest pain history → stress testing/echo workup even if now well. Refer cardiology.

subject: FM
stem: 70-year-old HTN, EF 65% on old echo, for elective non-cardiac surgery, asymptomatic. Pre-op?
options: A. Repeat echo + stress test in all
B. No routine echo; ECG + risk scores (RCRI) + optimise BP/meds; echo only if new murmur/HF
explanation: Normal EF on prior echo + currently asymptomatic with good functional capacity → no repeat echo. Follow ACC/AHA algorithm.

subject: FM
stem: Runner with pinpoint greater-trochanter pain, no trauma. Management?
options: A. Steroid injection first in all
B. NSAIDs + activity modification + physio (ITB/glute-med rehab); X-ray only if red flags
explanation: Greater-trochanteric pain syndrome: conservative first. Inject only if persistent; rule out hip OA/fracture if atypical.

subject: FM
stem: Woman lifting heavy: low-back pain radiating posterior leg, no red flags, neuro intact. Next?
options: A. Urgent whole-spine MRI in all
B. Stay active + analgesia + physio + red-flag safety-net; image only if persistent/neurologic
explanation: Acute sciatica without red flags: conservative 6 weeks. MRI if cauda equina, progressive deficit, cancer/infection suspicion.

subject: FM
stem: Known ankylosing spondylitis, sacroiliac pain, acute flare. Effective biologic class if NSAID fails?
options: A. Methotrexate always works in axial disease
B. TNF-alpha inhibitor (or IL-17) for active axial AS
explanation: Axial AS: NSAIDs + exercise first; TNF/IL-17 inhibitors for high activity. Methotrexate helps peripheral, not axial.

subject: FM
stem: Third-trimester bleeding: what most reduces mortality?
options: B. Abdominal US for placenta position + resuscitation + Rh + transfusion readiness; avoid PV if praevia suspected
C. IV fluids only without assessment
explanation: Never PV with suspected praevia – can provoke catastrophic bleed. Locate placenta abdominally, cross-match, steroids, C-section plan.

subject: FM
stem: Tingling lateral forearm + reduced brachioradialis reflex. Which nerve root?
explanation: C6: thumb/index, lateral forearm, biceps/brachioradialis. Know dermatomes/myotomes for EMREE.

subject: FM
stem: Healthy runner requests full-body MRI + antibiotics for viral cold. Best?
options: B. Explain risks/benefits, stewardship, shared decision-making; decline low-value care politely
explanation: Professionalism: avoid low-value testing/antibiotics, explain harms (incidentalomas, resistance), offer alternatives.

subject: FM
stem: Inter-professional conflict: nurse flags deterioration, junior dismisses. Best?
options: B. Structured handover (SBAR) + speak-up + early-warning score + escalate
explanation: Patient safety: graded assertiveness, SBAR, rapid response. Hierarchy never overrides safety.

subject: FM
stem: Suspected child/spouse/elder abuse with inconsistent story. Duty?
options: B. Private interview + thorough exam + document + mandatory report + safety plan per UAE law
explanation: Abuse: separate interview, body map, photos, report to authorities, admit if unsafe. Confidentiality yields to protection.
